stem: A new engineer at Pinecrest Labs runs `terraform login` with no arguments on a laptop that has never connected to HCP Terraform. What is the result?

choices.text: Terraform stores an encrypted token in the operating system keychain
Terraform obtains a token for `app.terraform.io` and saves it in plain text locally
Terraform writes the API token into the `cloud` block of the configuration file
Terraform refuses to continue until a hostname argument is supplied on the command line

rationale: Without an explicit hostname, Terraform assumes HCP Terraform at app.terraform.io, obtains an API token through a browser sign-in, and by default saves it in plain text in a local CLI configuration file called credentials.tfrc.json. An encrypted keychain entry is not the default behaviour. A token can be written in the `cloud` block, but the docs recommend omitting it, and `terraform login` does not do that. A hostname argument is optional because the default is app.terraform.io.
